newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: High level cocoa delegation heading for Abidjan.
newsitem.headline: High level cocoa delegation heading for Abidjan.

text.p: A delegation of cocoa industry representatives and lending officials will head for Ivory Coast next week to monitor progress on the country's privatisation programme, Dutch Cocoa Association director Louis Bensdorp said.

Bensdorp, part of the delegation alongside ICCO Executive Director Edouard Kouame and EU and World Bank lending officials, said the group would hold three-day talks with ministers as the first "The Cocoa Privatisation Committee" meeting.
"We are going to see what improvements have been made so far and what still needs to be done," Bendsorp told Reuters.
He said some of the concerns that had previously been raised included the cocoa bidding system and problems over quality.
In Abidjan, cocoa stock levels are believed to have been partly inflated by the electronic auction system, which is still unchanged in its first year despite demands for revision.

Industry sources there have said the system encourages exporters to hold back tonnages and sell at a higher premium. But whether or not it will be amended is doubtful. They noted that a visit by a European delegation in December had yet to bring about any change to the rules.
Bensdorp said another focus for the discussions would be consistent quality of exports, which caused problems for the European industry last year.
He said exporters holding back poor quality mid-crop cocoa and then mixing it in with main crop was a feature last year but the signs so far this season were that this had improved.
"We hope those days have gone but last year we also saw good cocoa to start with and then the quality became worse."
